![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14261151/assets/aa335a55f5b4496cdaccca5d35e286a168598761188bc520c81397ef136f927d.png)

Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is 

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<4,\,\bbox[5px,border:1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAA}}\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14261151/assets/fba9ba3e52ed19eb0bb2286ae59c49bb9dc648134d9eab3c4e2d13862963f736.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14261151/assets/2f3cd30dbaa4f84c43f2a7f1197aa904e3d43b1212241ae26736b2a0087f6170.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<4,\,0<y<2\}.
$$
